name: Kingsville
lede: Kingsville celebrates Christmas with La Posada de Kingsville, a free Children's Day and a Parade of Lights with more than 100 illuminated floats, plus a university Christmas concert.
celebrates: Kingsville keeps its holiday season anchored in downtown. Ranch Hand Weekend opens it in November with a Community Christmas Tree Lighting at 301 E Kleberg Ave, according to Visit Kingsville. On the first Saturday in December, La Posada de Kingsville brings Children's Day at the J.K. Northway Expo Center, a Parade of Lights down Kleberg Avenue and a weekend of music, vendors, food trucks and baking and wreath contests at the 1904 Train Depot. Texas A&M University-Kingsville adds a free Christmas Concert with choir, jazz, wind, string and mariachi groups.
lastyear: Visit Kingsville shows video from the 2024 La Posada de Kingsville: A Celebration of Lights, and describes the parade as tractors, trailers and trucks wrapped in Christmas lights and tinsel, with thousands of onlookers of all ages, according to its Texas Monthly feature. The 2026 page calls the festival 36 years in the making and says it always falls on the first Saturday in December. The 2026 Ranch Hand Weekend began on November 20 with the downtown tree lighting.
facts: Kingsville was founded in 1904 along the St. Louis, Brownsville and Mexico Railway, and the city's street directions are centered on the depot, according to a City of Kingsville planning document. Visit Kingsville says the depot museum opened on July 4, 2004, exactly 100 years after the city was chartered. The railroad was acquired by Missouri Pacific in 1925, and Union Pacific bought Missouri Pacific in 1982, the same document says.
trains: The 1904 Train Depot Museum at 102 E Kleberg Ave is free and open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm, according to Visit Kingsville. It tells how the St. Louis, Brownsville and Mexico Railway built the town, with lanterns, dining car place settings, railroad emblems and a working telegraph. The depot also hosts the La Posada weekend events on December 5 weekend. We did not find a Santa train or holiday train ride in Kingsville.
traditions: The Community Christmas Tree Lighting at 301 E Kleberg Ave opens the season in downtown Kingsville in November.
A Fiesta de Navidad on the first Saturday in December, with a Parade of Lights at 7 pm.
A free afternoon of activities for the youngest members of the community before the parade.
Live music, vendors, food trucks and baking and wreath decorating contests, listed by Visit Kingsville.
The La Posada committee arranges for Santa Claus to appear in the Parade of Lights.
kidfact: Kingsville was built around its railroad depot, and the town's streets are named for directions measured from that depot.
faq: When is the Kingsville Christmas parade?
La Posada de Kingsville holds its Parade of Lights on the first Saturday in December. In 2026 that is December 5 at 7 pm in downtown Kingsville, and Visit Kingsville lists it as free.
Where is the Kingsville parade route?
It starts at Kleberg Avenue and 11th Street by the courthouse, goes west on Kleberg Avenue and ends at 3rd and Kleberg by City Hall.
Is there a train to see in Kingsville?
The 1904 Train Depot Museum at 102 E Kleberg Ave is free to visit Tuesday to Saturday, 10 am to 4 pm. It is a railroad museum, not a ride, and we did not find a Santa train in town.
Is there something for little kids before the parade?
Yes. La Posada Children's Day runs from 10 am to 2 pm at the J.K. Northway Expo Center on the day of the parade, and Visit Kingsville lists it as free.
What starts the Kingsville holiday season?
Ranch Hand Weekend, held in late November, includes the Community Christmas Tree Lighting downtown at 301 E Kleberg Ave, according to Visit Kingsville.
